issues.description: The problem statement specifies a Book struct with properties named exactly 'title', 'author', and optional 'genres'. In the solution repository, the Book struct defines the title property as 'bookTitle' (let bookTitle: String) which conflicts with the expected 'title' name. This naming mismatch will confuse students about the correct property name to implement and causes client code that accesses 'book.title' to be inconsistent with the Book struct definition.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the Book struct property name from 'bookTitle' to 'title' (let title: String) in Sources/BookstoreLib/Bookstore.swift so it matches the problem specification and client usage. Update any references accordingly.

issues.description: The solution uses memberwise initializers for Book with parameter labels 'title', 'author', 'genres' (e.g., Book(title: ..., author: ..., genres: ...)) in assembleBookstore(), but the Book struct in the solution defines its title property as 'bookTitle', which produces a memberwise initializer labeled 'bookTitle' rather than 'title'. This creates a constructor parameter mismatch: the Book initializers used in Client do not match the actual memberwise initializer generated from the Book struct definition, preventing the code from compiling and confusing students about the expected initializer signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Ensure the Book struct's property names match the parameter labels used when creating Book instances. Either rename 'bookTitle' to 'title' in the Book struct so the memberwise initializer is init(title:author:genres:), or update all Book(...) calls to use the actual memberwise label 'bookTitle:'. Prefer renaming the property to 'title' to align with the problem description and expected API.

issues.description: The problem statement and expected API describe a Book with a 'title' and 'author' property, but the solution's Book struct declares the title field as 'bookTitle'. Meanwhile the solution's Client and Book initializations use the label 'title'. This inconsistent identifier for the same concept (the book's title) creates mapping confusion for students and can cause compile-time mismatches between initializers and property access.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the Book struct property 'bookTitle' to 'title' in solution_repository/Sources/BookstoreLib/Bookstore.swift so the memberwise initializer and property access align with the problem statement and Client usage; update any references accordingly (or alternatively change Client and initializers to use 'bookTitle', but aligning to 'title' better matches the problem description).
